artworks.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
artworks.description: On the shore of Naxos, Ariadne turns as Bacchus leaps from his cheetah-drawn chariot toward her — Theseus' ship already a pale sail on the horizon. The circle of stars above her head foreshadows the crown that will become the constellation Corona Borealis. Painted for Alfonso d'Este's camerino in Ferrara, the canvas now hangs in the National Gallery, London.

artworks.title: Sleeping Ariadne
artworks.artist: Unknown (Roman copy after a Hellenistic original)
artworks.description: The Vatican Museums' reclining marble shows Ariadne abandoned on Naxos — one arm thrown over her head, legs crossed, the serpentine bracelet on her arm long mistaken for Cleopatra's asp. A Hadrianic copy of a Pergamene Hellenistic type, it became one of antiquity's most famous statues and the model for countless later sleepers.

artworks.title: Bacchus, Venus and Ariadne
artworks.description: In the Doge's Palace, Tintoretto stages Ariadne's apotheosis: Bacchus rises from the sea with vine leaves and a marriage ring while Venus crowns the Cretan princess with stars. Commissioned for the Sala dell'Anticollegio, the square mythological canvas makes Ariadne the emblem of Venice favoured by the gods.

artworks.title: Ariadne Abandoned by Theseus
artworks.description: Kauffmann isolates the Naxos morning after the thread: Ariadne alone on the shore, Theseus' ship already gone, the emotional centre of Catullus' abandoned heroine restaged for a neoclassical audience. Oil on canvas, Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.

artworks.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
artworks.description: Gros returns to the Naxos meeting in the grand manner of French Romantic history painting: Bacchus' train surges toward the seated Ariadne as the island shore becomes a theatre of divine rescue. The canvas is held by the Phoenix Art Museum.

music.title: L'Arianna
music.description: Monteverdi's lost Mantuan opera survives in Ariadne's lament — the cry of the woman Theseus abandoned on Naxos, before Bacchus' arrival.

music.title: Ariadne auf Naxos
music.description: Strauss and Hofmannsthal nest the abandoned Ariadne inside a backstage comedy — the mythic heroine who must choose mourning or the god of wine.

music.title: Bacchus and Ariadne
music.description: Roussel's ballet for the Paris Opéra dances the Naxos rescue — Ariadne found by Bacchus after Theseus' sail has gone.

films.title: Minotaur, the Wild Beast of Crete
films.description: The peplum keeps Ariadne as the thread-giver: Minos' daughter who arms Theseus for the labyrinth and pays for it with exile.
